title: Graceful abort, reassembly, and cached-prefix reconciliation for interrupted streams
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement a robust flow-control and cleanup flow for partially-generated streaming responses. When clients disconnect, hit timeouts, or abort, the serving runtime should (1) gracefully drain or abort in-flight generation with minimal wasted GPU time, (2) publish compact reassembly metadata enabling clients to resume or reconcile partial outputs, and (3) reconcile/update the prefix/KV cache to avoid stale cached prefixes or duplicated tokens.
background: We observe repeated customer reports and internal telemetry where abrupt client disconnects lead to: 1) wasted token compute on resumed or orphaned generations, 2) cached prefix divergence where partial continuations corrupt later cached results, and 3) poor client UX when resuming sessions across unreliable networks. Existing work covers lease-based ownership and partial-output GC, but we need a cohesive reassembly and cache reconciliation strategy to reduce cost and enable smooth resume semantics across compatibility layers (HTTP/WS/GRPC).
acceptance_criteria: Server aborts or drains in-flight generation within configurable grace window and records a compact 'reassembly token' when partial output exists
Clients can resend a reassembly token to resume or reconcile generation; server validates and continues without double-producing tokens
KV/prefix cache entries updated or tombstoned to reflect partial output state; no cache corruption observed in integration tests
E2E tests cover disconnect during streaming, resume with reassembly token, and concurrent reconnects with conflicting tokens
Telemetry: 50% reduction in wasted token GPU time for disconnect-heavy workloads (measured in staged rollout)
design_notes: Reassembly token: small opaque blob (base64) containing generation-id, last-emitted-offset, short HMAC and optional client-supplied resume-hint. Token TTL defaults to 10 minutes.
Draining policy: configurable grace window (default 2s) during which we continue generation to deliver trailing deltas; after window, transition to fast-abort and snapshot KV cache state.
Two reconciliation modes for cache: tombstone-on-abort vs conservatively-mark-stale. Tombstone reduces wrong-reuse but increases cold-cache rate; conservative stale marking prefers availability.
Compatibility: HTTP chunked, WS delta-streams, and gRPC bidi must all surface reassembly token in a consistent header/pseudo-event to clients. Provide SDK helpers to parse and attach tokens.
Security: tokens signed per-customer key using runtime HMAC to prevent cross-tenant resume. Token contains no plaintext customer data.
Tradeoffs: aggressive tombstone improves correctness for structured output but increases downstream latency for first resumed requests; plan to gate tombstone by workload label and observe metrics.
implementation_steps: API: define 'x-reassembly-token' header and streaming pseudo-event 'REASSEMBLY_META' for delta streams
Runtime: emit reassembly token on client disconnect when partial output length > threshold (default 3 tokens)
KV cache: add 'stale_until' and 'abort_tombstone' flags, and compact GC logic to remove tombstones after token TTL
Resume flow: validate token HMAC, compare last-emitted-offset with server's model cursor, and resume with kernel state reuse when compatible
SDKs: add helper functions to attach tokens automatically with retries and to fallback to full new generation on mismatch
Testing: unit tests for token creation/validation, integration tests for WS/HTTP/gRPC flows, and chaos test that kills connections mid-stream
Metrics: add metric 'stream.wasted_tokens_on_disconnect' and dashboards showing wasted compute per customer and per model
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: tokens leak could allow resume replay across sessions. Mitigation: short TTL, per-tenant HMAC, optional one-time-use tokens for high-sensitivity tiers.
Risk: tombstone strategy increases first-request latency. Mitigation: rollout as opt-in per-customer and measure hit-rate before global switch.
Risk: resume incompatible when model rollout changed mid-token. Mitigation: include model-version in token and fallback to full regeneration on mismatch.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Internal dogfood on staging with SDKs for HTTP+WS, flag off tombstone mode (2 weeks)
Phase 2: Enable reassembly tokens for 5 pilot customers and collect metrics (4 weeks)
Phase 3: Gradual enablement with tombstone opt-in and per-tenant config (6 weeks)
Phase 4: Global default switch if KPIs met; add GA docs and console toggle
testing_notes: Create synthetic client that connects, streams partial tokens, then disconnects at random offsets. Verify token produced and resume path works across transport types.
Chaos job: kill GPU worker during a streaming generation and validate cache reconciliation and no double-emit on restart.
Load test: measure impact of tombstone marking on cache hit ratio and tail latency over a 72h window
